All 7 scenarios hold, so I wrote `{"findings": []}` to `findings.json`. I checked by reading the code, tests and specs. I ran no build, test or git command, so none of the tests have actually been run.

- **Manifest files read or refused:** `read_manifest` (`read/snapshot/folder.rs`) returns `Ok(None)` when the file is missing. It returns `StorageError::Read` for other I/O errors, such as a directory at the path. Text that doesn't parse returns `StorageError::Manifest`, whose message starts with the manifest's path. The typed `Manifest` struct accepts unknown keys and nulls, and refuses `[]`, `{"approvedAt": 5}` and notices without `items`. `tests/reading_manifest.rs` has one test per table row. On the base code the four refusal rows would read as `None` instead of failing, so those tests fail on the base.
- **Storage has no frontmatter parser of its own:** a search finds `YamlLoader` only in `read/snapshot/events.rs`, and `tests/reading_frontmatter.rs` checks the same thing.
- **The four read model rebuild scenarios:** `replace_read_model` builds into `<db>.rebuild`, renames it over the database only after the commit succeeds, and deletes the rebuild file if any step fails. `tests/read_model_atomic.rs` covers each scenario. One weak spot: the "path that cannot be replaced" test would also pass on the base code, because the old code already failed with `ReadModelError::Io` and left the directory in place. I didn't flag it, since the base already had that behavior.
- **Frontmatter the specs kernel refuses:** storage now goes through `osq_kernel_specs::parse_frontmatter`, which refuses YAML that isn't a mapping or doesn't parse. The base code accepted the list frontmatter `---\n- a\n---\nbody` and returned `body` alone, so the new test fails on the base.
